events.title: Emperor Claudius
events.description: Claudius becomes emperor. He expels Jews from Rome (ca. 49 AD) due to unrest around "Chrestus" – likely conflicts between Jews and Christians. Aquila and Priscilla leave Rome (Acts 18:2).

events.title: Claudius Expels the Jews from Rome
events.description: Claudius issues an edict expelling Jews from Rome. Suetonius notes it was due to unrest "at Chrestus' instigation," possibly a reference to Christ.

events.title: Emperor Nero
events.description: Nero becomes emperor. Initially a competent ruler under Seneca's guidance, he later develops into an unstable tyrant.

events.title: Seneca – Stoic Philosopher
events.description: Seneca, a Stoic philosopher and Nero's advisor, teaches about virtue, self-control, and universal brotherhood. Some have noted parallels to Pauline thought.

events.title: The Fire in Rome
events.description: A catastrophic fire ravages Rome for six days. Nero blames the Christians and initiates the first state-sponsored persecution. Peter and Paul are likely executed during this period.

events.title: Nero's Persecution of Christians
events.description: Nero persecutes Christians in Rome with brutal cruelty. They are thrown to lions, crucified, and used as living torches. The first systematic persecution of Christians.

events.title: The Jewish Revolt
events.description: Jews in Judea rise up against Rome. The Zealots take control of Jerusalem. Rome sends legions under Vespasian and later Titus to crush the rebellion.

events.title: The Destruction of Jerusalem
events.description: Titus's legions conquer and destroy Jerusalem, including the temple, on the 9th of Av (August) in 70 AD. Fulfillment of Jesus' prophecy in Matthew 24. Over one million Jews die according to Josephus.

events.title: Arch of Titus in Rome
events.description: The Arch of Titus is erected in Rome to celebrate the victory over Judea. The reliefs show Roman soldiers carrying the Temple's menorah and other sacred objects.

events.title: Eruption of Mount Vesuvius
events.description: The volcano Vesuvius buries the cities of Pompeii and Herculaneum under ash and lava. Pliny the Elder dies while attempting to rescue people. The cities are rediscovered in the 18th century.

events.title: Fall of Masada
events.description: The last Jewish fortress, Masada, falls after a long siege. According to Josephus, the 960 defenders commit mass suicide rather than surrender.

events.title: Josephus' historical works
events.description: The Jewish historian Josephus writes "The Jewish War" and "Jewish Antiquities." He mentions Jesus, James, and John the Baptist – important non-biblical sources.

events.title: Colosseum opens
events.description: The Flavian Amphitheater (Colosseum) in Rome opens with 100 days of games. It holds 50,000 spectators and is later also used for the execution of Christians.

events.title: Domitian's persecution of Christians
events.description: Emperor Domitian demands to be addressed as "Lord and God" and persecutes Christians who refuse the imperial cult. The apostle John is exiled to Patmos during this period.

events.title: Pliny's letter about the Christians
events.description: Pliny the Younger writes to Emperor Trajan on how to handle Christians in Bithynia. The letter offers a unique insight into early Christian practice from an outside perspective.

events.title: Tacitus confirms the execution of Christ
events.description: The Roman historian Tacitus mentions in his Annals that "Christus" was executed under Pontius Pilate during the reign of Tiberius – an important extra-biblical source.
